before.question: Which statement is most accurate? Focus: virus natural history.
choices: HCV is an enveloped positive-sense RNA virus whose error-prone replication creates diversity, chronic infection, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma risk.
Assuming asymptomatic infection is harmless delays curative therapy.
Use one result without reviewing fibrosis, prior treatment, interactions, coinfection, or liver compensation.
Assume every DAA combination, genotype, and cirrhosis state is interchangeable.
before.rationale: HCV is an enveloped positive-sense RNA virus whose error-prone replication creates diversity, chronic infection, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma risk. Connect duration, fibrosis, alcohol, metabolic disease, HIV, age, and treatment history to progression risk.

after.question: Which statement is most accurate? Focus: virus natural history.
choices: HCV has a positive-sense RNA genome, and persistent infection can cause progressive fibrosis and cirrhosis
HCV is a DNA virus that must be diagnosed with HBV DNA
Normal ALT excludes clinically significant HCV-related fibrosis
The RNA concentration alone establishes the degree of cirrhosis
after.rationale: HCV is an RNA virus. Persistent infection can cause progressive liver injury, but progression varies; symptoms, ALT and viral load do not replace fibrosis staging. Genetic diversity is not itself a clinical fibrosis score.
